text:
alex: Heads up — we saw a ~30% throughput drop on MQA Llama-70b when paged KV is enabled on dedicated-1. p50 stable but p90 and tokens/sec tanked. Looks like kernel selection is switching away from our fused attention path to the slower fallback. Anyone dug into a heatmap or trace yet?

perf-bot: [regression] perf anomaly detected on dedicated-1 (2026-03-18T14:11Z). Metric: tokens/sec down 28% vs baseline, affected model: llm-mqa-70b-v2, route: /v1/generate.

maya: I generated a KV occupancy heatmap and a kernel-choice timeline. Heatmap shows fragmentation concentrated on slab-pages 3..7 (non-contiguous occupied slots). Kernel timeline: fused_attn_v2 -> attn_loop fallback spikes exactly when fragmentation > 22%. Paste of heatmap legend + small snippet below.

maya: ```
# kv layout summary (sampled)
occupied_pages = [0,1,4,5,6,9,12]
free_runs = [2,3,7,8,10,11]
fragmentation_score = 0.27
kernel_choice = [fused_attn_v2, fused_attn_v2, attn_loop, attn_loop, attn_loop, fused_attn_v2]
```

ron: quick question — what's the num_key_value_heads and kv_dim we used for this build? Could mismatch between heads and layout packing be causing misalignment that forces a different kernel?

alex: For Llama-70b-MQA we compile with num_key_value_heads=32 and kv_dim = 128 per-head. Qwen profiles were using 16 historically. The fused kernel assumes contiguous kv slabs per num_heads chunk. If slabs get interleaved, the kernel can't use its vectorized load.

maya: profiling traces backpressure: GPU memory loads are non-coalesced when stride between adjacent slots > 256 bytes. That triggers the kernel selector to mark layout as "nonoptimal" which forces the attn_loop path. I added a tiny microbenchmark: when eviction_stride <= 128 coalescing is ok, but current autoscaler/evict-policy uses 256 for paged KV.

sam: Proposed short experiments:
- Set eviction_stride=128 for a canary and monitor fused_attn_v2 fallback rate
- Add a compaction pass that coalesces recently-freed small runs into contiguous chunks (sticky compactor)
- Try interleaved->coalesced layout switch for MQA-only pool
Would prefer to run compactor in read-only/validation first.

jin: Ran a 1-hour canary on dedicated-2 with eviction_stride=128 + compactor=off: result +12% tokens/sec, p90 down ~90ms. Logs snippet: ```
[14:22:01] pick_kernel fused_attn_v2 (contiguous)
[14:22:01] throughput 9.8k tok/s -> baseline 8.7k
[14:22:01] gpu_util 72% -> baseline 79% (less waiting)
```

maya: I also instrumented RoPE offsets for Mixtral experiments — not the culprit here but worth noting: RoPE scaling can change memory access patterns (because we pack rotary caches differently) and sometimes nudges the fragmentation threshold earlier. For Mixtral/Qwen we should add a RoPE-aware packing sanity check.

alex: Plan: open two PRs — (A) compactor smoke patch + unit tests for packing invariants, (B) config toggle to set eviction_stride per-pool (default old value). Canary rollout: 10% traffic on dedicated-1 for 2 hours, monitor kernel fallback rate and tokens/sec. Rollback: flip eviction_stride back and disable compactor.

ron: If compactor looks safe, consider applying coalescing during low-load windows only to avoid CPU spikes. Also add metric exported: fraction_contiguous_kv_pages to console dashboard.

sam: Also add an e2e perf test (simulated MQA multitenant) that asserts no kernel-fallback regressions under 20% fragmentation. Save baseline artifacts.

alex: I'll create the PRs and the dashboard panel. Assigning: maya -> heatmap + RoPE sanity check, jin -> canary run + logs, sam -> e2e harness, ron -> dashboard + metric.

perf-bot: deploy-bot: canary started on dedicated-1 (config: eviction_stride=128, compactor=false) at 2026-03-18T15:05Z. Monitoring channels: eng-runtime + eng-sre.

alex: Thanks all — quick sync in 30 to review canary numbers. :thumbsup:
